name: Nashville depot, 3 MW service + Megapack storage
notes: The founder's site-acquisition thesis made runnable: take a 3-5 MW site plus storage instead of holding out for a 10 MW site. Three Tesla Megapack 2 XL (3,000 kWh / 1,500 kW each, LFP, 96% RTE, SoC 10-95%) from ottoq_bess_units -- real specs, not invented. Firm capacity during a wave is 3,000 + 4,500 = 7,500 kW, but ONLY for as long as the energy lasts: 7,650 kWh usable / 4,500 kW = 1.70 h. That duration limit is the correction recorded in docs/BESS_SITE_ACQUISITION_THESIS.md -- storage is sized by ENERGY, not power, and a 4-hour wave needs ~4.7 packs, not 3. Recharge counts toward the same monthly peak, so the recharge is itself a scheduling problem. Field precedent for the pattern: Zenobe/National Express Yardley Wood, 667 kWh BESS serving 19 e-buses on a restricted grid connection (R-4).

tariff.notes: From the NES commercial-rate PDF, already held in ottoq_depot_tariffs. Demand basis is 30-minute NCP -- a Southeast regional trait (R-5), NOT a default. Energy rate 4.785 c/kWh is the base excluding the TVA fuel cost adjustment (~2.8-4 c/kWh), so total energy cost is understated here by design; the FCA is a pass-through that varies monthly.
